findings.source_passage: 'Bles-sed pre-cious,' she crooned... 'Come to your own mother that loves you.' ... 'The bles-sed pre-cious! Did mother get powder on your old yellowy hair?'
findings.why_it_matters: The Pammy scene's signature weight is in Daisy's performative baby-talk and the 'You dream, you. You absolute little dream' line — Fitzgerald's indictment of Daisy's maternal performance. Draft keeps one crooning line and drops the 'dream' line entirely, flattening one of the chapter's key character-evidence passages.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'You dream, you. You absolute little dream' exchange and at least one more of Daisy's crooning lines with Pammy.

findings.source_passage: 'I got dressed before luncheon,' said the child... 'Yes,' admitted the child calmly. 'Aunt Jordan's got on a white dress too.'
findings.why_it_matters: Pammy's calm, literal replies are the reality against which Daisy's performance registers. Cutting them removes the ironic contrast the scene depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least Pammy's 'Aunt Jordan's got on a white dress too' reply and the 'Come, Pammy' / 'Goodbye, sweetheart!' beat.

findings.source_passage: 'I know I'm not very popular. I don't give big parties. I suppose you've got to make your house into a pigsty in order to have any friends—in the modern world.'
findings.why_it_matters: This is Tom's self-pitying pivot — the pigsty/modern-world sneer that completes the libertine-to-prig transition Nick explicitly names in the next paragraph. Without it, Nick's 'transition from libertine to prig' observation loses its antecedent.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Tom's 'I know I'm not very popular...' speech verbatim before Nick's 'transition from libertine to prig' line.

findings.source_passage: 'That's a good idea,' I got up. 'Come on, Tom. Nobody wants a drink.'
findings.source_locator: Plaza, just before Gatsby's 'Your wife doesn't love you'
findings.why_it_matters: Nick's small intervention is a rare moment of narrator agency in the scene; its loss is minor but thins the texture.

findings.source_passage: 'Of course it matters. I'm going to take better care of you from now on.' ... 'As if it mattered to you,' she said.
findings.source_locator: Plaza, between Daisy's 'Even alone I can't say I never loved Tom' and Gatsby's 'You're not going to take care of her any more'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'take care of her' exchange is the logical hinge for Gatsby's immediately following 'You're not going to take care of her any more' — without it Gatsby's line dangles.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Daisy/Tom 'As if it mattered to you' / 'I'm going to take better care of you' exchange.

summary: Draft preserves the chapter's heavy signatures (heat opening, 'voice full of money,' golden girl, Plaza hinges, 'dead dream,' thirty, 'toward death through the cooling twilight,' Myrtle's death, 'watching over nothing') faithfully; the losses are in the Pammy scene texture and Tom's pigsty line, which together rise to three medium findings but no high — borderline pass.
